cards.question: What are the three-flare drills and objective?
cards.answer:
Find first-stage flare sweet spot: identify tandem pair penduluming under canopy nose; two-stage flare looking forward; repeat two-stage flare with eyes closed.

Official-manual comparison [COURSE-ONLY DETAIL]: OPS endorses and requires briefing the canopy proficiency framework, but does not independently reproduce this exact drill sequence/numeric detail. The supplied UPT card remains the detailed source. IRM p.163 supports a sweet-spot demonstration, but not the eyes-closed repetition specifically.
References: OPS p.13; OPS p.14; IRM p.163

cards.question: What is the forced-recovery drill?
cards.answer:
Aggressive 90–180-degree turn; neutralize turn then immediately symmetric flare, “match & finish”; repeat opposite direction. Objective: simulate collision/obstacle avoidance.

Official-manual comparison [COURSE-ONLY DETAIL]: OPS endorses and requires briefing the canopy proficiency framework, but does not independently reproduce this exact drill sequence/numeric detail. The supplied UPT card remains the detailed source. OPS restricts turns greater than 90 degrees below 500 feet and predictable flight below 1,000; the high-altitude drill is not a low-altitude avoidance authorization.
References: OPS p.13; OPS p.14; OPS p.50; OPS p.52
Ask evaluator: Confirm drill sequence, brake system, altitude margin, stall avoidance and traffic supervision before rehearsal.

cards.question: What is the repositioning-over-ground drill?
cards.answer:
Hold three-quarter brakes; while in deep brakes turn 90 right, 90 left, 90 left, 90 right to original heading. Also called sashay, S-turn, or quad 90s; objective mid-pattern repositioning for accuracy.

Official-manual comparison [COURSE-ONLY DETAIL]: OPS endorses and requires briefing the canopy proficiency framework, but does not independently reproduce this exact drill sequence/numeric detail. The supplied UPT card remains the detailed source. OPS discourages braked/stall-surge normal approaches; the training maneuver does not authorize low pattern S-turns.
References: OPS p.13; OPS p.14; OPS p.50; OPS p.52
Ask evaluator: Confirm drill sequence, brake system, altitude margin, stall avoidance and traffic supervision before rehearsal.

cards.question: How do you assess altitude loss in turns?
cards.answer:
360-degree full-input turn then full flight, note altitude loss; repeat with quarter input, note altitude loss.

Official-manual comparison [DIFFERENCE FOUND]: The card's general 2,000-foot completion rule does not override OPS's no-360-turns-below-2,500-foot rule.
Manual guidance: Complete both 360-degree exercises above 2,500 feet AGL with sufficient start altitude for altitude loss; the card supplies the full-input/quarter-input drill details.
References: OPS p.50
Ask evaluator: Confirm both 360 drills must finish above 2,500 feet and identify their start-altitude margin.

cards.question: What stacking and communication exercises are listed?
cards.answer:
Compare descent rates; use half brakes to increase vertical separation; pass on-level canopies using full-input turns; ideally establish canopy order by 2,000 feet/600 meters.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Descent-rate/stacking specifics remain card-sourced. OPS additionally mandates at least 100 feet canopy separation; passing drills cannot be treated as permission to violate separation.
Manual guidance: Maintain at least 100 feet canopy separation and predictable flight. Use the card's stacking exercises only under a briefed supervised traffic plan.
References: OPS p.13; OPS p.14; OPS p.68
Ask evaluator: Confirm drill sequence, brake system, altitude margin, stall avoidance and traffic supervision before rehearsal.

cards.question: What preparation and accuracy requirements are listed?
cards.answer:
Rehearse canopy dive flows on ground before jumping; landing accuracy as directed in Tandem Instructor Logbook.

Official-manual comparison [PARTIAL SUPPORT / OMITTED DETAILS]: Accuracy remains referred to the UPT Logbook; IRM has separate rubric anchors of safe effective landing within 82 feet for Good and 60 feet for Excellent. These are not standalone overall pass/fail thresholds.
Manual guidance: Use the UPT Logbook requirements for UPT drills; separately apply the IRM landing rubric and brief the actual target. Ground rehearsal remains supported by the course framework.
References: OPS p.13; OPS p.14; IRM p.203

cards.question: What if safety concerns or unforeseen circumstances prevent drill completion?
cards.answer:
No repeat jumps necessary, but candidates are encouraged to complete all drills before final endorsement. Safety first.

Official-manual comparison [VERIFIED]: Safety constraints preventing drill execution do not automatically disqualify candidate; all skills must still be briefed. This does not waive separate USPA air/supervision evaluations.
References: OPS p.13; OPS p.14

cards.question: What if the candidate is under a reserve?
cards.answer:
Concentrate solely on landing priorities and dismiss the briefed canopy dive flow.

Official-manual comparison [QUALIFIED / CONTEXT]: Reserve landing priorities are consistent with the manual; dismissal of the assigned drill flow is explicitly card-sourced.
Manual guidance: Prioritize safe reserve canopy control and landing; instructor-only reserve controls, no secondary toggles; address reserve problems and seek slowest/softest landing. Card says dismiss planned drill flow.
References: OPS p.55; OPS p.56
